subject: Week 18: finalize the allergen-introduction plan before solids
bodyText:
This week
Days 124-130 sit mid-stretch between the 4-month vaccines and the 6-month milestones: brief tripod sitting, one-handed reaching, and consonant babble (ba, da, ga) with vocal turn-taking are the headline developments. Rolling both directions is emerging for some - the CDC checkpoint for rolling tummy-to-back is 6 months, so its absence now is not a flag. Socially he distinguishes you from strangers and anticipates being picked up.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Teething signs - drool, gum-rubbing, chewing everything, extra fussiness. Symptoms front-run the first tooth by weeks; eruption typically waits until 6-10 months.
- [monitor] Night sleep not consolidating 4-6 weeks past regression onset despite a stable routine and environment - log the wakings and bring the log to the 6-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Persistent or worsening eczema - it moves him into a higher allergen-introduction risk tier, and that conversation must happen before peanut does.
- [call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher, fewer than five wet diapers in 24 hours, labored breathing, or blue lips or unresponsiveness - 911 for breathing or color change.

Enrichment opportunities
- Finalize the allergen plan by risk tier: severe eczema or known egg allergy means a pediatric allergist before peanut; mild eczema or family history means a pediatrician conversation about a 4-6-month start per the LEAP-derived guidelines; no risk factors means peanut arrives around 6 months with other solids. AAP - Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Protect open floor time - rolling practice is organic now, with him flipping in and out of tummy time on his own. Keep container time (seats, swings) to a minimum during wake windows. AAP - Movement: 4 to 7 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-4-to-7-Months.aspx
- Anchor the post-regression bedtime routine: bath, feed, book, song - same order nightly, drowsy-but-awake into the crib, bedtime in the 18:00-19:00 slot. Most infants consolidate within 2-6 weeks of a consistent response strategy. AAP - Getting Your Baby to Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Book the first-birthday photographer - top SF milestone photographers book 4-6 months out, which puts a May 2027 session inside the booking window now.

Upcoming
- Day 112-126 (Aug 31-Sep 14, 2026): 4-month well visit - window closes Monday; if it has not happened yet, book today.
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26-Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit - book now. Vaccines: RV #3 (if RV5), DTaP #3, Hib #3 (if PRP-T), PCV #3, influenza #1; iron/hemoglobin screen; solids-readiness assessment.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses voice to express joy and displeasure
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Distinct vocalizations for different states — early affective communication.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-voice-for-joy/complete

- Rolls from back to tummy
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Harder direction; requires more core and upper-body strength.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/rolls-back-to-tummy/complete

- Reaches for objects with one hand
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Differentiation from earlier two-handed swiping — emerging hand preference is normal but unstable until ~age 3.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/reaches-with-one-hand/complete

- Pushes up with straight arms during tummy time
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Full arm extension, chest off the floor. Builds toward sitting.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/leans-on-hands-tummy-time/complete

- Leans on hands to support self when sitting
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Tripod sit. Precedes hands-free sitting by 1-2 months.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-with-hand-support/complete
